title: Freelancer Success Principles
tips: [{"heading":"Treat It Like a Business","body":"Register properly, track income and expenses from day one, and set aside tax quarterly. The freelancers who fail usually treat financial administration as an afterthought until it becomes a crisis."},{"heading":"Always Use Contracts","body":"A simple contract protects both parties. Define scope, payment terms, revision limits, and IP ownership before work begins. A verbal agreement is not a contract — it is a misunderstanding waiting to happen."},{"heading":"Niche Down Early","body":"Generalists compete on price. Specialists compete on expertise. A clear niche — an industry, technology, or problem type — makes you easier to refer, price, and find."},{"heading":"Build a Referral System","body":"Most freelancers' best clients come from existing clients. A simple ask — 'if you know anyone who needs this, I would appreciate an introduction' — costs nothing and compounds over time."}]
